source: Canadian National Autism Foundation, cnaf.net/provinceres.html; each entry checked on its own website

entries.name: Programs for Persons with Disabilities (NL Department of Health and Community Services)
entries.description: Newfoundland and Labrador's health department funds disability programs delivered by NL Health Services, including the Special Child Welfare Allowance for families of children with disabilities, the Special Assistance Program for medical equipment and supplies, home support (including respite), therapeutic and professional services, and residential options for adults. Its Intervention Services include the home-based Direct Home Services early intervention program, an Intensive Applied Behaviour Analysis program for children with an autism diagnosis (up to Grade 3), and Community Behavioural Services.
entries.cost_note: Mixed: the Direct Home Services Program is provided at no cost to the family; other programs use financial needs tests or subsidies.
entries.evidence: The Direct Home Service Program also includes an Intensive Applied Behaviour Analysis Program for children with a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder.
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://www.health.gov.nl.ca/health/personsdisabilities/index.html; that now redirects to https://www.gov.nl.ca/hcs/personsdisabilities/ (an overview), and this page describes the programs. CNAF's text refers to the four Regional Health Authorities; the page now names NL Health Services, and each program says to contact NL Health Services in your area. CNAF also links to the department's old contact page (Regional Health Authorities).

entries.name: Newfoundland and Labrador Prescription Drug Program (NLPDP)
entries.description: A provincial program that helps residents of Newfoundland and Labrador pay for eligible prescription medications and some related supplies, through five plans (Foundation, 65Plus, Access, Assurance and Select Needs). It pays only when costs are not covered by another insurer, and each plan has its own eligibility rules.
entries.cost_note: Coverage and co-pays depend on the plan and family income; the Foundation Plan needs no application.
entries.evidence: The Newfoundland and Labrador Prescription Drug Program (NLPDP) provides financial assistance for the purchase of eligible prescription medications for those who reside in the province.
entries.notes: CNAF links to an anchor on the department's old contact page (health.gov.nl.ca), which now redirects to the general contact page; the program's own current page is used here. The phone number is from the How do I Apply? page (Access Plan applications).

entries.name: Dental Health Plan (NL Department of Health and Community Services)
entries.description: Newfoundland and Labrador's public dental coverage. The Children's Dental Health Program covers basic dental care for all children up to and including age 12; other programs cover basic services for youth and adults in income support or low-income households, and medically necessary surgical dental care.
entries.cost_note: Covers eligible services only; the page suggests parents ask their dentist whether a recommended treatment is covered.
entries.evidence: The Children’s Dental Health Program provides universal access to eligible dental services for children up to and including 12 years of age.
entries.notes: CNAF lists "Dental Services" with an old P.O. Box / Major's Path address and links to the department's old contact page; the program's current page is used here. Youth (13-17) and adult programs depend on income support or NLPDP Access/Foundation Plan enrolment; the phone number is the NLPDP line given on the page for eligibility. The page also points to the federal Canadian Dental Care Plan.

entries.name: StudentAidNL
entries.description: Newfoundland and Labrador's student loan and grant program for post-secondary students, run with the federal government; one application assesses students for both. Students with disabilities can also apply for the Canada Student Grant for Services and Equipment (up to $20,000 per year for costs such as tutors, note-takers or technical aids) and, if needed, the Provincial Grant for High Need Students with Disabilities.
entries.cost_note: Loans and grants; the site does not mention an application fee.
entries.evidence: With one application, StudentAidNL will assess you for both federal and provincial financial assistance.
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://www.aes.gov.nl.ca/studentaid/ and its old disability forms; those no longer work (404). The program now uses https://www.gov.nl.ca/education/studentaid/. Office at 95 Elizabeth Avenue, St. John's; the disability grant forms are on the Forms and Documentation page.

entries.name: Human Rights Commission (Newfoundland and Labrador)
entries.description: A free service for people in Newfoundland and Labrador who feel they have been discriminated against or harassed: they fill out an online inquiry form, and the Commission reviews requests and handles complaints through early resolution, mediation or hearings. It also gives human rights information, presentations and training.
entries.cost_note: The site says the Commission is a free service.
entries.evidence: The Newfoundland and Labrador Human Rights Commission is a free service that is available to people in Newfoundland and Labrador.
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://www.justice.gov.nl.ca/hrc/; that no longer works (it redirects to the Justice and Public Safety home page). The Commission now uses https://thinkhumanrights.ca/. Local phone 709-729-2709; the site says responses can take time because of high volume.

entries.name: Office of the Child and Youth Advocate (Newfoundland and Labrador)
entries.description: An independent office of the Newfoundland and Labrador House of Assembly that stands up for the rights and interests of children and youth under 19 (up to 21 for those who have been in care or custody) in their dealings with child-serving systems. It offers individual and systemic advocacy, investigates and reviews complaints, and teaches about children's rights.
entries.cost_note: The FAQ says no referral is necessary and there is no cost.
entries.evidence: We offer individual advocacy, systemic advocacy where groups of young people are affected, and we investigate and review complaints and offer education on children’s rights.
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://www.childandyouthadvocate.nf.ca/; that now redirects to the office's current domain, https://www.childandyouthadvocate.nl.ca/. Toll-free 1-877-753-3888. The office is at 20 Crosbie Place in St. John's (the footer says Suite 205, the FAQ says Suite 103) but serves the whole province, much of it by phone.

entries.name: Speech Language Pathology Private Practice (SLPPP)
entries.description: A private speech-language pathology clinic in St. John's, with a second location in Clarenville and online services across Newfoundland and Labrador, offering assessment and therapy for all ages. Its speech-language pathologists work with autistic children and with language delay, speech clarity, stuttering, reading and other communication difficulties.
entries.cost_note: Rates vary by length, type and location of service (call for rates); covered by most insurance plans and tax deductible.
entries.evidence: Our comprehensive, family-focused services include assessment and treatment of the full range of communication difficulties.
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://www.speechtherapynl.ca/en/, which is now a 404; the practice's home page (https://www.speechtherapynl.ca/) is current. Self-referral is accepted, and the FAQ says appointments are usually available within a week. Clarenville location: 105 Manitoba Drive.

entries.name: Newfoundland and Labrador Association of Speech-Language Pathologists and Audiologists (NLASLPA)
entries.description: A not-for-profit professional association of speech-language pathologists and audiologists in Newfoundland and Labrador. For the public, it explains what these professionals do and keeps a Find a Professional directory of private-practice speech-language pathologists, with each one's location, populations treated and areas of interest (several list autism).
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost; each listed practitioner sets their own fees.
entries.evidence: Champions the interests of those who require speech, language, swallowing, hearing, and balance services
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://www.nlaslpa.ca/pg.php?p=1, which is now a 404 on the same site; the association's current pages are used. Mailing address P.O. Box 21212, St. John's. The association's own listed email is a Gmail address (not a person's).

entries.name: First Light
entries.description: A registered charity, formerly the St. John's Native Friendship Centre, that serves the city's urban Indigenous and non-Indigenous community. It offers housing, justice and social supports, health services such as Indigenous patient navigation, medical transportation and wellness counselling, help with Jordan's Principle and Inuit Child First, childcare and family resource programs, and cultural events.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Formerly known as the St. John’s Native Friendship Centre, First Light is a registered charity & non-profit organization dedicated to revitalizing & celebrating Indigenous cultures & languages.
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://www.sjnfc.com/ (St. John's Native Friendship Center); that now redirects to https://firstlightnl.ca/, and the About page confirms the name change. Headquarters at 70 Brookfield Road, with other locations around St. John's.

entries.name: Legal Aid NL
entries.description: Provides family and criminal law services to people with low incomes in Newfoundland and Labrador, through Legal Aid lawyers in offices around the province. Applicants must qualify financially and have a type of legal matter Legal Aid covers; some administrative matters, such as social assistance and Mental Health Review Board appeals, may also be covered.
entries.cost_note: For people who qualify financially; the site does not say whether clients pay anything.
entries.evidence: Legal Aid provides a range of legal services to low income individuals in Newfoundland and Labrador in the areas of family and criminal law.
entries.notes: CNAF lists Legal Aid with no link, only two phone numbers (709-489-9081 and 709-639-9226); the Contact page shows these are its Grand Falls-Windsor and Corner Brook area offices. Provincial office: Suite 300, 251 Empire Ave, St. John's.

entries.name: Attendant Pass (City of St. John's)
entries.description: A City of St. John's card for a person with a disability who needs a support person to take part in community events and activities. With the pass, the attendant gets in free or at a discount at accepting venues such as City facilities and events, Metrobus, The Rooms and the Arts and Culture Centre.
entries.cost_note: The attendant gets in free or at a discount set by each venue; the page does not mention a fee for the pass.
entries.evidence: The pass enables an attendant or support person to accompany a person requiring support to activities and/or events for free or at a discounted rate determined by the accepting venues.
entries.notes: CNAF links to an old stjohns.ca URL that is now 404; the City now uses this page. A medical professional, social worker or disability agency must verify the application; apply by email, by mail, or in person at the H.G.R. Mews Community Centre (60 Blacker Ave). Processing takes 2 to 4 weeks.

entries.name: Easter Seals Newfoundland & Labrador
entries.description: A St. John's-based organization with programs for people with disabilities of all ages, including recreation programs, summer camps for children, socials and family events, employment and educational services, and equipment programs (an equipment loan program and Linda's Equipment Crossing).
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Our mission is to engage, inspire, and maximize opportunities for people with disabilities of all ages by providing meaningful programs and services.
entries.notes: CNAF's link (http://www.eastersealsnl.ca/index.php) now lands on https://eastersealsnl.ca/; the program subpages returned 403 to our fetcher, so details come from the home page only. Toll-free 1 (877) 754-1399. CNAF lists it under Financial Support (help with wheelchairs, ramps and other equipment).
